title: What is a micro-credential?
description: A micro-credential certifies assessed learning from a short course. How the Australian framework and the 2022 EU Council Recommendation define it.
shortAnswer: A micro-credential is a certification of assessed learning from a small volume of study, smaller than a full qualification, that records specific learning outcomes a person has achieved. Australia's National Microcredentials Framework defines it as certifying assessed learning or competency with at least one hour of learning, and a 2022 Council of the European Union Recommendation defines it as a record of assessed learning outcomes that the learner owns and can share and combine into larger credentials.
keyTakeaways: A micro-credential certifies assessed learning; attendance alone does not qualify under either the Australian or the EU definition.
Australia's National Microcredentials Framework (March 2022) sets a minimum of one hour of learning and less than a full Australian Qualifications Framework award.
The EU Council Recommendation of 16 June 2022 lists mandatory elements, including learning outcomes, notional workload, type of assessment, and type of quality assurance.
Micro-credentials can stand alone or be stacked toward larger credentials where a provider recognizes them for credit.
A micro-credential evidences learning against stated outcomes; it does not by itself prove competence in a specific workplace role.

sections.heading: How do official frameworks define a micro-credential?

blocks.text: Official definitions agree on three features: a small volume of learning, clearly stated learning outcomes, and assessment against those outcomes. They differ in detail, so check which framework applies where a credential will be used.

items: **Australia.** The [National Microcredentials Framework](https://www.education.gov.au/higher-education-publications/resources/national-microcredentials-framework), published by the Australian Government education department in March 2022, defines microcredentials as "a certification of assessed learning or competency, with a minimum volume of learning of one hour and less than an AQF award qualification" that is additional, alternate, complementary to, or a component part of an AQF award qualification.

**European Union.** The [Council Recommendation of 16 June 2022 on a European approach to micro-credentials for lifelong learning and employability](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022H0627%2802%29) defines a micro-credential as "the record of the learning outcomes that a learner has acquired following a small volume of learning", assessed against transparent and clearly defined criteria. It adds that micro-credentials are owned by the learner, can be shared and are portable, may be stand-alone or combined into larger credentials, and are underpinned by quality assurance.

blocks.text: The EU text is a Council recommendation, which guides member states rather than binding them. The Australian framework is a national framework, not legislation; providers apply it voluntarily or as a condition of specific programs.

sections.heading: What information should a micro-credential include?

blocks.text: Both frameworks require enough information for an employer or education provider to understand what was learned, how it was assessed, and how much learning it represents.

sections.heading: How is a micro-credential different from microlearning or a completion certificate?

blocks.text: A micro-credential is a credential: a certified record of assessed outcomes. [Microlearning](/glossary/microlearning) is a delivery format of short learning units, which may or may not lead to any credential. A completion certificate usually records participation, not assessed achievement.

sections.heading: Can micro-credentials evidence competence in regulated roles?

blocks.text: They can contribute evidence, but they rarely replace workplace assessment. A micro-credential shows that a person achieved stated learning outcomes in an assessed course; it does not show they can apply that learning to your procedures, equipment, and risks.

items: **Check the outcomes and assessment.** Compare the credential's stated learning outcomes and assessment type with the competence the role requires. Both frameworks require these to be stated, which makes the comparison possible.

**Use it for knowledge, verify skills locally.** A micro-credential can evidence underpinning knowledge; observed workplace assessment or [verification of competency](/glossary/verification-of-competency) usually still applies to the task itself.

**Treat it like any prior learning.** Many organizations handle external credentials through a [recognition of prior learning](/glossary/recognition-of-prior-learning) process, recording what was accepted and why.
**Watch currency.** A credential records learning at a date. If the underlying rule or method has changed, the credential may no longer cover the current requirement.

blocks.title: Illustrative example
blocks.text: A new data protection officer holds a micro-credential in privacy regulation with stated outcomes and an assessed case study. The employer accepts it as evidence of underpinning regulatory knowledge, records the decision in its competence register, and still assesses the person on the organization's own breach response procedure before authorizing them to lead an incident. The scenario is illustrative.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry expresses training as defined learning outcomes linked to assessment points and provenance, which is the information micro-credential frameworks ask issuers to state. That makes it possible to compare an external credential's outcomes with a role's requirements point by point. See [standards and accreditation](/platform/standards-accreditation).

faqs.q: Is it spelled micro-credential or microcredential?
faqs.a: Both are used. The EU Council Recommendation uses "micro-credential" with a hyphen, while Australia's National Microcredentials Framework uses "microcredential" as one word. The meaning is the same. Use the form of the framework you are applying, and be consistent within a document.

faqs.q: Can micro-credentials be stacked into a qualification?
faqs.a: Sometimes. Both frameworks allow micro-credentials to be stand-alone or combined toward larger credentials, but stacking depends on an education provider recognizing them for credit. Australia's framework asks issuers to state where credit applies only when micro-credentials are stacked together.

faqs.q: Can an employer issue its own micro-credentials?
faqs.a: Yes. The EU Recommendation lists employers and industry among possible providers. Credibility depends on stated learning outcomes, genuine assessment, and quality assurance. An internally issued micro-credential that meets those elements is more useful to the holder and to future employers than a simple completion certificate.

Creation date 22 March 2022, Department of Education, Skills and Employment.

Council Recommendation of 16 June 2022 (2022/C 243/02), paragraph 5(a) definition; providers include employers and industry; Annex I mandatory elements: learner identification, title, issuer country, awarding body, date, learning outcomes, notional workload (ECTS where possible), level (EQF, QF-EHEA) if applicable, type of assessment, form of participation, type of quality assurance; optional stackability.
